title: GS21 with a PRODUCTIVITY-CURVATURE exposure: one type, production x exp(+0.2 (z~^2 - 1) y), z~ the standardized idiosyncratic productivity (U-shaped), price 2.5
question: Does a y exposure that is quadratic in the firm's own productivity, mean zero across firms, give GS21 a non-monotone premium that no linear sort holds and DKKM a gap?
notes:
WHY (2026-10-30). The leverage-curvature version (gvyql10/20, gvyqh10) failed because the leverage characteristic spans only 0.002-0.006 across quintiles; productivity has the cross-sectional variation and is revealed by ROE and size. The reduced form's pure-curvature loading on observed characteristics (kfh_sq_1) has room 647% and a gap of +0.52: this is its structural counterpart, with the curvature in the exposure to a priced y.

DESIGN. gs_bzz (new) adds gs_bv * gs_bzz * (z~^2 - 1) to the exposure multiplier; gs_bzl 0 so there is no level exposure; bv_comp 0 (one type, no shift). gs_bzz = 0 leaves every other economy unchanged (x + 0.0).

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-10-30): room 30-60% of the linear ceiling (the y Sharpe sits almost entirely outside the linear span), fair gap +0.03 to +0.10. FALSIFIED if room is below 11% (gvy25s) or the gap below +0.01 on three seeds.

changes: gs_bzq 1 -> 0 (dropped); gs_bzz 1 (new); gs_bv 0.2; everything else gvyql10's

method.gs_ashift_ladder: derived: -bv_comp log W(gs_bv), applied in solver and simulator
method.gs_vy_sign_ladder: mirrored level-exposure ladder, E[gs_bv] = 0 across types, each type level-compensated at y = 0

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks (global numpy stream) and the AGGREGATE state path (gam_seed / bx_seed / reg_seed offset by the seed). Seed 0 reproduces the single-run behaviour; --common_aggregate restores the fixed-aggregate behaviour as an explicit variance decomposition.
